<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par128 />{{GHGmargin-letter|128|p}}
(''i'') Of the ''attribute'' of a person or thing, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם|translate=an everlasting possession}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=17|verse=8}} ''a precious stone''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=28|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=23|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=31|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=5|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=19}}, and the examples of the genitive with a suffix given in {{GHGpar|135|n}}. Such a periphrasis for the expression of attributes frequently occurs, even when the corresponding adjectives are in use. Thus especially {{GHGheb|text=קֹ֫דֶשׁ|translate=holiness}} very frequently serves as a periphrasis for the adjective {{GHGheb|text=קָדוֹשׁ}} (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בִּגְדֵי הַקֹּ֫דֶשׁ|translate=the holy garments}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=29}}), since {{GHGheb|text=קָדוֹשׁ}} is used almost exclusively in reference to persons (hence also with {{GHGheb|text=עַם}} and {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹי|translate=people}}, and with {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁם}} the ''name'' of a person); the only exceptions are {{GHGheb|text=מָקוֹם קָדוֹשׁ|translate=holy place}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=31}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫יִם קְדשִׁים|translate=holy water}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=קָדוֹשׁ}} as the predicate of {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם|translate=day}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=8|verse=10}} f., and of {{GHGheb|text=מַֽחֲנֶה|translate=camp}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=23|verse=15}}. So also the use of {{GHGheb|text=צַדִּיק|translate=righteous}} is always confined to persons, except in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=8}}; elsewhere the periphrasis with {{GHGheb|text=צֶ֫דֶק}} or {{GHGheb|text=צְדָקָה}} is always used, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מֹֽאזְנֵי צֶ֫דֶק|translate=just balances}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=19|verse=36}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|q}}
In a wider sense this use of the genitive also includes statements of the purpose for which something is intended, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צֹאן טִבְחָה|translate=sheep for the slaughter}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=מוּסַר שְׁלוֹמֵ֫נוּ|translate=the chastisement designed for our peace}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=5}}; cf. 51:17 (''the cup which causes staggering''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=13}}; finally, also, the description of the material, with which something is laden or filled, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=חֲמֹר לֶ֫חֶם וְנֹאד יַ֫יִן|translate=an ass}} laden ''with bread and a bottle of wine'' (but probably {{GHGheb|text=עֲשָׂרָה}} is to be read for {{GHGheb|text=חֲמֹר}}); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=7|verse=20}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|r}}
Rem. 1. Certain substantives are used to convey an attributive idea in the construct state before a partitive genitive; thus {{GHGheb|text=מִבְחָר|translate=choice, selection}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=מִבְחַר קְבָרֵ֫ינוּ|translate=the choice of our sepulchres}}, i.e. our choicest sepulchres; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=24|hidebook=1}}; other examples are, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=16}} ''the evil of your doings'', emphatically, for ''your evil doings''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=24|hidebook=1}} (=''the tall cedars thereof''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=26}}.—This is the more common construction with the substantive {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל|translate=entirety}}, for ''all, the whole, every'', see {{GHGpar|127|b}}; it is also frequent with {{GHGheb|text=מְעַט|translate=a little}}, for ''few'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=28}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|s}}
2. To the periphrases expressing attributive ideas (see p above) by means of a genitive construction may be added the very numerous combinations of the construct states {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ|translate=a man}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּעַל|translate=master, possessor}}, {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־|translate=son}}, and their feminines and plurals (including {{GHGheb|text=מְתֵי|translate=men}}, used only in the plural), with some appellative noun, in order to represent a person (poetically even a thing) as possessing some object or quality, or being in some condition. In English, such combinations are sometimes rendered by single substantives, sometimes by circumlocution.

Examples:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|t}}
(''a'') Of {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ דְּבָרִים|translate=an eloquent man}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=10}} (but {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ שְׂפָתַ֫יִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=2}} ''a man of lips'', i.e. ''a boaster''); {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ לָשׁוֹן}} = ''a slanderer'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=140|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ דַּ֫עַת|translate=a man of knowledge}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ חֵמָה|translate=a wrathful man}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=15|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ דָּמִים|translate=a man of blood}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=7}}; cf. further, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=19|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=29|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=8|verse=18}}; also {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫שֶׁת מִדְיָנִים|translate=a contentious woman}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=15}}; in the plural, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=אַנְשֵׁי הַשֵּׁם|translate=the men of renown, famous}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=8}}, 10 ({{GHGheb|text=אַנְשֵׁי לֵבָב|translate=men of understanding}}); with {{GHGheb|text=מְתֵי}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=13}} ({{GHGheb|text=מְתֵי רָעָב|translate=famished men}}; but read probably {{GHGheb|text=מְזֵי רָעָב|translate=weak with hunger}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=26|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=15|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|u}}
(''b'') Of {{GHGheb|text=בַּ֫עַל}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=בַּ֫עַל שֵׂעָר|translate=hairy}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=1|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּ֫עַל הַֽחֲלֹמוֹת|translate=the dreamer}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=19}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=18|verse=9|hidebook=1}} (''a destroyer''), 22:24, 23:2 (''disposed to eat, greedy''), 24:8; feminine<section end=par128 /><noinclude>
